title: Oxygen-deficiency bands and carbon dioxide exposure limits
source: OSHA 29 CFR 1915.11 and OSHA's 2 April 2007 interpretation letter to FirePASS Corporation for oxygen; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory EHS table for graded effects; NIOSH Pocket Guide to Chemical Hazards entry for carbon dioxide.
rows: OSHA 29 CFR 1915.11 definition: 'an atmosphere having an oxygen concentration of less than 19.5 percent by volume'
The 2007 letter treats anything below 19.5 percent as immediately dangerous to life or health.
Oxygen level at which impaired judgement is reported
LBL: below 15 percent, 'impaired attention, impaired judgement, impaired coordination'; OSHA letter: at 10 to 14 percent 'faulty judgment, intermittent respiration, and exhaustion'
Value and High are LBL's 15 percent; Low is the bottom of OSHA's 10 to 14 band. The sources differ on the band. LBL also reports reduced night vision below 17 percent and dizziness below 16.
Oxygen level at which loss of consciousness is reported
LBL: below 12 percent, 'loss of consciousness, permanent heart or brain damage possible'; below 10 percent 'unconsciousness'; OSHA letter: 6 to 10 percent 'perhaps unconsciousness'
Value and High are LBL's 12 percent; Low is the bottom of OSHA's 6 to 10 band. Exposure time and exertion are not stated.
Oxygen level at which convulsions and death are reported
LBL: below 6 percent, 'spasmodic breathing, convulsive movements, death in 5-8 minutes'; OSHA letter: convulsions, then apnea, then cardiac standstill
Carbon dioxide NIOSH recommended exposure limit, time-weighted average
NIOSH Pocket Guide, REL TWA for a 10-hour work shift of a 40-hour week
The page text read for this unit gave 'TWA 5000 ppm (9000 mg/m3)'; the period (10 h) is the Pocket Guide's usual definition, not read from the page.
Carbon dioxide NIOSH short-term exposure limit
Short-term period (15 min) is the Pocket Guide's usual definition, not read from the page.
Carbon dioxide immediately dangerous to life or health
Carbon dioxide OSHA permissible exposure limit, 8-hour time-weighted average
OSHA PEL as listed in the NIOSH Pocket Guide: 'TWA 5000 ppm'
